title: Family Card pilot reaches 74,259 families; national survey under way
excerpt: The Family Card pilot paid Tk 2,500 a month to 74,259 families by September. Data on 59 lakh of an estimated 4.1 crore households has been collected for the full rollout.
content:
The government's Family Card cash programme reached 74,259 families in its pilot phase between March and September, the Ministry of Social Welfare told the parliamentary standing committee on the ministry on Thursday (26 November), Prothom Alo reported. Under the scheme, a woman in each selected family receives Tk 2,500 a month.

The ministry said data were collected from 112,094 households in 55 wards of 42 districts across all eight divisions between February and June. Using a proxy means test (PMT), a score of a household's social and economic condition, it selected 77,894 women for the card. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman formally launched the programme on 10 March.

For the full programme, planned for the 2026-27 financial year, a survey of every household in the country, about 4.1 crore, began on 12 October and is due to end in December. About 70,000 enumerators and supervisors have been hired and 66,815 tablets handed out. Data on 59,16,796 households had been collected by 23 November, the ministry said.

Payments go straight to the beneficiary's mobile wallet or bank account. Sonali, Janata, Krishi and Pubali banks have been brought in to open accounts and issue cards, and money can be drawn at ATMs, point-of-sale machines and mobile financial services agents. Grameenphone and Robi have been given separate areas to provide SIM cards and internet access to beneficiaries.

The committee told the ministry to make sure that genuinely poor and vulnerable families are chosen and that selection, data checks and payments are transparent and accountable, according to a parliament secretariat release. The ministry said it had repeat checks and public hearings in place to make sure cards go to the right people. The Daily Star also reported the figures.

Why it matters

Family Card is set to become one of the largest cash transfers in Bangladesh, and its targeting will decide who gets help. A World Bank review found that half of the poorest households get no safety net at all. NGOs working with poor women, people with disabilities and char and haor communities will want to know whether the PMT reaches people who are often missed by household surveys, and how complaints will be handled. Payment through mobile wallets also depends on women owning phones and accounts, a gap shown in the Bangladesh Bank financial inclusion report.

What to watch

  • Whether the household survey finishes in December as planned.
  • The selection criteria and PMT cut-off for the national rollout, and whether they are published.
  • The budget allocation for 2026-27 and how complaints and appeals will work.
